intent.raw_query: Hawaii family beach vacation, $5000, 10 days, August 2026 from Seattle

selected_hotel.name: Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most iconic marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with colorful fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters and equipment rentals on-site. An educational visitor center teaches about the reef ecosystem before you enter.

experiences.name: Luau Dinner at Paradise Cove
experiences.description: Experience an authentic Hawaiian luau right on the beachfront with traditional hula dancing, fire knife performances, and a feast of local dishes including kalua pig, poi, and fresh tropical fruits. A magical cultural evening the whole family will remember, with activities like canoe rides and lei making before the show.

experiences.name: Catamaran Sunset Sail with Whale Watching
experiences.description: Board a family-friendly catamaran for a breathtaking sunset cruise along the Waikiki coastline. During winter and spring months, spot humpback whales breaching offshore. The crew provides snacks, drinks, and narration about Hawaiian marine life, making it both entertaining and educational for children and adults alike.

experiences.name: North Shore Shrimp Trucks and Beach Day
experiences.description: Spend a full day on Oahu's legendary North Shore, starting with a stop at the famous roadside shrimp trucks for garlic butter shrimp plates — a beloved local food tradition. Then relax on the wide sandy shores of Sunset Beach or Waimea Bay, where gentle summer waves are perfect for family swimming and building sandcastles.

experiences.name: Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach
experiences.description: Take a beginner group surfing lesson with certified instructors right on the gentle waves of Waikiki, considered the birthplace of modern surfing. Lessons are tailored for all ages including young children, and most first-timers stand up on their board within the first session. Boards and rash guards are included in the price.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Hawaii
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most iconic marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with colorful fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters and equipment rentals on-site. An educational visitor center teaches about the reef ecosystem before you enter.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Flight arrives, clear customs, collect baggage.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, take TheBus Route 23 or a shared shuttle from the airport to Hanauma Bay area (budget-friendly ~$3 bus fare). Check into the Hanauma Bay East Oahu Boutique Stay, freshen up, and take a short leisurely walk along nearby Kalaniana'ole Highway coastal path to stretch your legs and get your first glimpse of the Pacific Ocean. Visit the nearby Sandy Beach Park (free entry) to dip your toes in the sand and acclimate to island life.
day_by_day.evening: Head to nearby Koko Marina Center for a casual first dinner. Try Zippy's Restaurant — a beloved local Hawaii chain offering affordable plate lunches, saimin noodle soup, and chili rice bowls for under $12 per person. Pick up snacks and breakfast items at the Times Supermarket in Koko Marina for the next morning to save money throughout the trip.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport meal
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Honolulu Airport's food court or pack snacks for the ride (~$8–$12)
meals.dinner: Zippy's at Koko Marina Center — plate lunch or saimin bowl (~$10–$14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Buy a reloadable HOLO card for TheBus at the airport or a nearby 7-Eleven — single rides are $3, unlimited monthly passes available. Stock up on groceries tonight to save significantly on breakfasts throughout the trip. Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations for snorkeling — book online tonight for a future day.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast at the hotel using groceries purchased last night (cereal, fruit, yogurt — ~$3 per person). Then head to Makapu'u Point Lighthouse Trail (free entry) — a 2-mile round-trip paved trail with breathtaking panoramic views of the Windward Coast, sea cliffs, and offshore islands. Arrive early (7:00–8:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. Great for families with kids — stroller-accessible path.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or bus to Makapu'u Beach Park (free entry), located just below the lighthouse. This is one of Oahu's top bodysurfing beaches. Families with younger children should wade carefully and watch the waves — lifeguards are on duty. Pack a picnic lunch from your grocery supplies. Spend 2–3 hours swimming, building sandcastles, and enjoying the stunning scenery including the offshore Rabbit Island.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel area and cook a simple dinner using groceries (sandwiches, pasta, or rice with canned goods). Alternatively, visit L&L Hawaiian Barbecue at Koko Marina for affordable plate lunches served all day (~$10–$13). End the evening with a sunset stroll along the coast near your hotel.

meals.breakfast: DIY hotel breakfast — cereal, fruit, juice from grocery store (~$3 per person)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic at Makapu'u Beach — sandwiches, chips, fruit (~$4 per person)
meals.dinner: L&L Hawaiian Barbecue at Koko Marina or simple grocery cook-in (~$10–$13 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Bring reef-safe sunscreen, hats, and plenty of water for the lighthouse hike. The trail has no shade. Makapu'u Beach has strong shore break — supervise children closely. Confirm Hanauma Bay reservation online tonight if not done yesterday.

day_by_day.morning: Today is Hanauma Bay Snorkeling Day! Reservations required — arrive at your designated entry time (aim for the 7:00–8:00 AM slot to see the most fish and avoid midday crowds). Entry fee is $25 per adult, children under 12 are free. Watch the mandatory marine education video, then spend 2–3 hours snorkeling among hundreds of tropical fish including parrotfish, surgeonfish, and sea turtles in the protected bay. Snorkel gear rental available on-site (~$12–$15).
day_by_day.afternoon: After Hanauma Bay (closes at 1:30 PM on Tuesdays — verify current hours), head to nearby Koko Head Crater Trail for a more adventurous afternoon. This famous 1,048-step railway tie staircase hike offers spectacular 360-degree views of East Oahu. Note: This is strenuous — best for older kids and teens. Younger children can enjoy the adjacent Koko Head District Park (free) with playgrounds and open fields.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the day's adventures with dinner at Ono Seafood, a legendary local poke shop near Koko Marina area — fresh ahi poke bowls are ~$13–$16 and are absolutely worth every cent. This is an authentic local experience. Pick up shave ice from a nearby stand for dessert (~$4–$6).

meals.breakfast: DIY hotel breakfast — toast, peanut butter, bananas (~$2–$3 per person)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and water for Hanauma Bay — no outside food allowed inside the bay area, but you can eat at the facility's snack bar (~$8–$12) or eat before/after
meals.dinner: Ono Seafood poke bowl (~$13–$16 per person) + shave ice dessert (~$4–$6)

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay is closed on Tuesdays — IMPORTANT: double-check the current closure schedule before booking. If Tuesday is a closure day, swap this day with Day 4. Hanauma Bay has limited parking ($3) — arriving by TheBus (Route 22) is recommended and saves money. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only — chemical sunscreens are banned at Hanauma Bay.

day_by_day.morning: Take TheBus toward Waikiki (Route 22/23, ~45 min, $3 each way). Spend the morning exploring Waikiki Beach (free). Walk the famous beachfront strip, let the kids play in the gentle waves, and watch the surfers. The beach is calmer and more family-friendly than East Oahu beaches. Rent a bodyboard from a beach vendor (~$10/hour) or just enjoy the sand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Kapiolani Park (free) — Hawaii's largest public park. Enjoy the open lawns, watch local sports games, and visit the Honolulu Zoo which is adjacent (budget option: $20 adults, $12 children — or skip for the free park). Alternatively, walk through the park to Diamond Head State Monument entrance and enjoy views of the famous crater from the outside (free). Pack a picnic lunch to eat in the park.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Waikiki for dinner — visit the International Market Place food hall for affordable options. Try Giovanni's Shrimp Truck (a famous North Shore brand with a Waikiki outpost) or grab plate lunches from local vendors (~$12–$15). Catch the free nightly hula and live music performances on Kalakaua Avenue (check schedule). Take TheBus back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: DIY hotel breakfast (~$3 per person)
meals.lunch: Picnic in Kapiolani Park — grocery-prepared sandwiches, fruit, drinks (~$4 per person)
meals.dinner: International Market Place food hall, Waikiki (~$12–$16 per person)

day_by_day.notes: TheBus is the most budget-friendly way to reach Waikiki. The trip takes about 45 minutes from East Oahu. Free hula shows happen most evenings at the Kuhio Beach Hula Mound — check the City & County of Honolulu website for exact times. Waikiki is walkable and very family-friendly.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or bus to Diamond Head State Monument for a morning hike (parking $10/car or TheBus Route 23, $3). The 1.6-mile round-trip trail inside the volcanic crater leads to a summit with sweeping views of Waikiki and the Pacific. There are tunnels, spiral staircases, and bunkers that kids love to explore. Entry fee: $5 per person. Start by 7:00–8:00 AM for cooler temperatures. Reservations required — book online in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Diamond Head, head back toward East Oahu and stop at Alan Davis Beach (Kawaiku'i Beach Park) — a quieter, less-touristy beach near your hotel perfect for a relaxed afternoon swim. Pack a picnic lunch. Spend 2–3 hours relaxing, swimming in calmer waters, and enjoying the local beach atmosphere away from tourist crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Try a local favorite for dinner: visit Keneke's BBQ in Hawaii Kai for authentic Hawaiian plate lunches — lau lau, kalua pig, poi, and rice for around $12–$15 per plate. This is a genuine local experience. End the evening with a walk to the Hawaii Kai Marina waterfront to watch the sunset over the Koolau Mountains.

meals.breakfast: DIY hotel breakfast (~$3 per person)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic at Alan Davis Beach (~$4 per person)
meals.dinner: Keneke's BBQ, Hawaii Kai (~$12–$15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head reservations are required and slots fill up fast — book at least 2–3 days ahead at hawaiistateparks.org. Bring water and snacks for the hike. The trail has 175 steps and some narrow passages — manageable for most children over age 5. Flashlights or phone lights are helpful for the tunnels.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the North Shore! Catch TheBus (Route 55 or 52 via transfer, ~2 hours, $3 each way) or rent a car for the day (~$50–$70 with insurance). Visit Waimea Valley (entry: $20 adults, $10 children) — a lush botanical garden with a beautiful 45-foot waterfall and swimming hole at the end of a 0.75-mile walk. This is one of the best family-friendly nature experiences on Oahu. The valley is culturally significant and the walk is easy and shaded.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Waimea Valley, walk to nearby Waimea Bay Beach Park (free) — one of Hawaii's most iconic beaches. In summer, the bay is calm and perfect for swimming and snorkeling. In winter it has massive surf, but August conditions should be ideal for families. Grab shave ice at nearby Matsumoto Shave Ice in Haleiwa (~$4–$6) — a legendary North Shore institution since 1951.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Haleiwa Town — the charming surf town hub of the North Shore. Browse local shops, grab dinner at Kono's Northshore (~$10–$14 for burritos and plates — a local favorite) or pick up fresh fish tacos from a food truck along Kamehameha Highway. Head back to the hotel via bus or car, arriving by 8:00–9:00 PM.

meals.breakfast: DIY hotel breakfast — pack extra snacks for the long day (~$3 per person)
meals.lunch: Picnic at Waimea Bay or grab plate lunch from a North Shore food truck (~$10–$13)
meals.dinner: Kono's Northshore or Haleiwa food truck (~$10–$14 per person) + Matsumoto Shave Ice (~$4–$6)

day_by_day.notes: The North Shore day trip is long — leave by 7:30–8:00 AM to maximize time. If taking TheBus, the journey requires a transfer and takes about 2 hours each way — plan accordingly. Renting a car for this day gives much more flexibility. Check surf conditions at Waimea Bay before swimming — even in summer, shore break can be strong.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Pali Lookout (Nu'uanu Pali State Wayside) — a dramatic cliffside overlook with views of the Windward Coast and the Ko'olau Mountains (free entry, $7 parking). The winds here are famous and thrilling for kids. Learn about the historic 1795 Battle of Nu'uanu. Then drive down the Pali Highway to the Windward side of Oahu to explore a different landscape — lush, green, and dramatically beautiful.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kailua Beach Park on the Windward Coast (free) — consistently ranked one of the best beaches in the United States. The water is calm, turquoise, and perfect for families. Rent kayaks from Kailua Beach Adventures (~$30–$40/hour for a double kayak) and paddle toward the Mokulua Islands offshore, or simply swim and relax on the white sand. Explore the charming Kailua town for local shops and boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Kailua town — try Cinnamon's Restaurant for early dinner (known for Hawaiian-style breakfast/brunch served all day, ~$12–$18 per person) or grab affordable plate lunches from Kalapawai Market deli (~$10–$14). Head back to the hotel via the Pali Highway.

meals.breakfast: DIY hotel breakfast (~$3 per person)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic for Kailua Beach or grab from Kalapawai Market (~$8–$12 per person)
meals.dinner: Cinnamon's Restaurant or Kalapawai Market deli, Kailua (~$10–$18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Kailua Beach is on the Windward side — a car is strongly recommended for this day. Parking at Kailua Beach Park is free but fills up on weekends — arrive before 9:00 AM. The Pali Lookout can be very windy — secure hats and lightweight items. Kailua town has a wonderful local farmers market on Sundays if you want to shift this day.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Kailua Sunday Farmers Market (if you shifted Day 7 activities, otherwise visit the KCC Farmers Market near Diamond Head — Saturdays 7:30–11:00 AM, free entry). Stock up on fresh local fruits, malasadas (Portuguese donuts), and local snacks at very affordable prices. Spend the late morning at a relaxed beach — return to Sandy Beach Park near your hotel for a low-key morning of swimming and sunbathing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Koko Head area on foot — visit Halona Blowhole Lookout (free, roadside pull-off on Kalaniana'ole Highway) where ocean swells shoot water dramatically through a lava tube. Just a short drive from your hotel. Then visit the small Halona Beach Cove (the 'From Here to Eternity' beach) — a stunning hidden cove accessible via a short trail down the cliff. Great for photos and a quick swim in calm conditions.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed Sunday evening with a grocery-prepared dinner at the hotel or nearby beach. Consider a simple Hawaiian BBQ using a free public grill at a beach park — a very local Sunday tradition. Alternatively, pick up fresh poke from Foodland Farms at Koko Marina (~$13–$16/pound) and enjoy it as a poke bowl dinner with rice from your grocery supplies.

meals.breakfast: Farmers market treats — fresh fruit, malasadas, local pastries (~$6–$10 per person)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic at Sandy Beach or Halona Cove (~$4 per person)
meals.dinner: DIY poke bowl from Foodland Farms + grocery rice and sides (~$10–$14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Halona Blowhole is best viewed after a large swell — check surf reports. Never stand near the blowhole opening — it can be dangerous. Halona Beach Cove has a steep trail — use caution with young children. The cove can have strong currents; check conditions before swimming. Public BBQ grills at beach parks are free to use — bring your own charcoal.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Pearl Harbor National Memorial — one of Hawaii's most important historical sites and a moving educational experience for the whole family. Take TheBus (Route 20 or 42, ~1 hour, $3 each way) or drive (~30 min from East Oahu). The USS Arizona Memorial boat tour is free but requires timed-entry passes (reserve online in advance at recreation.gov — $1 reservation fee). Arrive early as passes are limited. The visitor center, exhibits, and memorial are deeply impactful.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the additional Pearl Harbor sites — the USS Bowfin Submarine Museum ($15 adults, $8 children) is an excellent hands-on experience kids love, allowing them to climb through a real WWII submarine. The Pacific Aviation Museum ($25 adults, $15 children) is optional if budget allows. Spend 1–2 hours at the site before heading back toward the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Stop in the Ala Moana area on the way back for dinner at the Ala Moana Center food court — one of the largest malls in Hawaii with dozens of affordable dining options including Asian cuisines, Hawaiian plate lunches, and fast casual restaurants (~$10–$15 per person). Browse the free outdoor mall and enjoy the evening atmosphere before heading home.

meals.breakfast: DIY hotel breakfast — pack snacks for the long day (~$3 per person)
meals.lunch: Pearl Harbor Visitor Center café or packed lunch (~$8–$12 per person)
meals.dinner: Ala Moana Center food court (~$10–$15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor reservations are essential — book the USS Arizona Memorial timed-entry pass weeks in advance, especially in summer. No bags larger than 1 gallon are allowed at Pearl Harbor — leave backpacks in the car or use the paid bag check service. The experience is solemn and educational — prepare children beforehand about the historical significance.

day_by_day.morning: Last morning in Hawaii — enjoy a final sunrise walk along the East Oahu coastline near your hotel. Revisit your favorite nearby beach for a farewell swim. Pack up belongings and check out of the hotel. If time allows, stop at the Lanai Lookout on Kalaniana'ole Highway (free roadside stop) for one last panoramic view of the Pacific Ocean and the rugged lava coastline — a stunning final memory of East Oahu.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, head toward the airport with time to spare (Honolulu Airport is ~30–40 minutes from East Oahu by car, or ~1 hour via TheBus Route 23). If you have extra time before the flight, browse the airport's local shops for affordable souvenirs — look for Honolulu Cookie Company outlet, local macadamia nuts, and Kona coffee as budget-friendly gifts. Duty-free shopping is also available for international travelers.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Honolulu. Aloha and safe travels! Carry the spirit of Hawaii home with you.

meals.breakfast: Final DIY hotel breakfast or a treat at a local café — try Kalapawai Café & Deli if open on your route (~$8–$12 per person)
meals.lunch: Light meal at airport or grab a final plate lunch to-go from a nearby spot before heading to the airport (~$10–$14 per person)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security at Honolulu Airport, especially during busy summer season. Return any rental car with a full tank of gas to avoid expensive refueling fees. TheBus does not accommodate large checked luggage — take a taxi or rideshare ($35–$45) if you have big bags. Consider buying extra shave ice or a final poke bowl as your last taste of Hawaii!

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Settle in after landing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay. After freshening up, take a leisurely stroll along the shoreline near Hanauma Bay to get your bearings and soak in the scenery. Pick up snacks and essentials at a nearby convenience store.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Koko Marina Center for a relaxed first dinner. Explore the waterfront area and enjoy the sunset views over the marina.

meals.breakfast: Grab something at the airport or on the plane before landing.
meals.lunch: Pick up plate lunches or poke bowls from a local deli or food truck near the hotel upon arrival (~$12–18/person).
meals.dinner: Kona Brewing Company at Koko Marina — casual waterfront dining with fresh seafood, burgers, and local craft beers (~$20–35/person).

day_by_day.notes: Flight arrives at 13:00. Allow 60–90 minutes for baggage claim, car rental or shuttle, and the drive to East Oahu. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel. Reserve snorkeling gear at the hotel front desk for tomorrow morning.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — Explore one of Hawaii's most iconic marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with colorful tropical fish and sea turtles. Arrive early (7:00–8:00 AM) to secure entry reservations and beat the crowds. Watch the mandatory marine education video before entering the bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: After snorkeling, rinse off and drive to nearby Halona Blowhole Lookout and Sandy Beach for a scenic coastal stop. Relax on the sand or watch bodyboarders tackle the shore break. Walk the bluffs for dramatic ocean views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to freshen up, then head out for a family-friendly dinner in the area.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel or grab acai bowls and smoothies from a nearby café before heading to Hanauma Bay (~$10–15/person).
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch or grab plate lunches from a food truck near Hanauma Bay — spam musubi, macaroni salad, and fresh fruit (~$10–15/person).
meals.dinner: Ono Hawaiian Foods in Kaimuki — beloved local spot for authentic Hawaiian cuisine including kalua pig, laulau, and poi (~$15–25/person).

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance online reservations ($25/adult, free for Hawaii residents and children under 13). The bay is closed on Tuesdays. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, water shoes, and plenty of water. Snorkel gear can be rented on-site or at the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Since Hanauma Bay is closed on Tuesdays, explore Diamond Head State Monument. Hike the iconic 1.6-mile round-trip trail to the summit crater for panoramic views of Waikiki and the Pacific Ocean. Start early to avoid heat (7:00–8:00 AM). Kid-friendly with moderate effort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive into Waikiki and spend the afternoon on Waikiki Beach. Build sandcastles, swim in the calm waters, and people-watch along the famous strip. Browse the beachfront shops and pick up souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach — Take a beginner group surfing lesson with certified instructors right on the gentle waves of Waikiki. Evening lessons are often less crowded and the golden-hour light makes it magical for photos.

meals.breakfast: Cinnamon's Restaurant in Kailua — famous for their red velvet pancakes and local-style breakfast (~$15–22/person).
meals.lunch: Marukame Udon in Waikiki — budget-friendly Japanese udon noodles in a cafeteria-style setting, always a hit with families (~$8–12/person).
meals.dinner: Duke's Waikiki — iconic beachfront restaurant named after Duke Kahanamoku, serving fresh fish, burgers, and Hawaiian favorites with ocean views (~$25–40/person).

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head reservations recommended online ($5/person, $10/car). Bring water and sunscreen for the hike. Surfing lessons typically run 1.5–2 hours; book in advance with a reputable school like Hans Hedemann Surf School (~$50–75/person for group lessons).

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the Windward Coast and visit Kailua Beach Park — consistently ranked one of the best beaches in the US. Enjoy calm, turquoise waters perfect for swimming, kayaking, and paddleboarding. Rent kayaks to paddle out to the Mokulua Islands offshore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming town of Kailua. Browse boutique shops along Kailua Road, visit the Kailua Farmers Market (if available), and enjoy the laid-back local atmosphere. Stop at Lanikai Beach for a quick visit to one of Oahu's most picturesque stretches of sand.
day_by_day.evening: Return to East Oahu for a relaxed evening. Enjoy a sunset walk near the hotel and a casual dinner close to home base.

meals.breakfast: Kalapawai Café & Deli in Kailua — beloved neighborhood café with excellent pastries, sandwiches, and coffee (~$10–18/person).
meals.lunch: Buzz's Original Steakhouse in Kailua — a Kailua institution right across from the beach, offering burgers, fresh fish, and salads in a casual setting (~$18–30/person).
meals.dinner: Keneke's BBQ in Hawaii Kai — local plate lunch spot with Hawaiian BBQ, kalbi ribs, and teriyaki chicken near the hotel (~$12–20/person).

day_by_day.notes: Kayak rentals in Kailua run approximately $25–45 for a half-day. The paddle to Mokulua Islands takes about 30–45 minutes each way and is suitable for families with older children. Apply waterproof sunscreen generously — the Windward side can be sunnier than expected.

day_by_day.morning: North Shore Shrimp Trucks and Beach Day — Start early and drive up to Oahu's legendary North Shore. Stop at Giovanni's Shrimp Truck or Romy's for the famous garlic butter shrimp plates. Browse the roadside stalls and enjoy the relaxed North Shore vibe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the North Shore beach day at Sunset Beach or Ehukai Beach Park (home of the Banzai Pipeline). In August the waves are calm and perfect for swimming and snorkeling. Walk the shoreline and look for sea turtles resting on the sand at Laniakea Beach (Turtle Beach) on the drive back.
day_by_day.evening: Stop at Haleiwa town on the way back for shave ice at Matsumoto's — a North Shore tradition. Browse the surf shops and galleries before heading back to East Oahu.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel before the drive, or stop at a bakery in Haleiwa on the way up.
meals.lunch: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck or Romy's Kahuku Prawns — iconic roadside shrimp trucks with garlic butter, spicy, or lemon pepper shrimp plates (~$15–18/plate).
meals.dinner: Koko Head Café in Kaimuki — trendy brunch-all-day spot with creative Hawaiian-inspired dishes, open for dinner on select days, or opt for nearby local favorites (~$18–28/person).

day_by_day.notes: The drive from East Oahu to the North Shore takes approximately 60–75 minutes. Plan to leave by 8:00–9:00 AM. Laniakea Beach turtle viewing is a highlight — stay behind the rope barriers and never touch the turtles. August is the calm season on the North Shore, making it ideal for families.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Bishop Museum in Honolulu — Hawaii's premier natural and cultural history museum. Explore exhibits on Hawaiian royalty, ancient Polynesian navigation, and natural science. The planetarium show is excellent for families and adds an educational dimension to the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Ala Moana Beach Park — a long, calm, reef-protected beach perfect for families. Swim, relax in the shade, and enjoy the beautiful park setting. Afterward, browse Ala Moana Center, the largest open-air shopping mall in the US, for souvenirs and treats.
day_by_day.evening: Catamaran Sunset Sail with Whale Watching — Board a family-friendly catamaran for a breathtaking sunset cruise along the Waikiki coastline. Enjoy light snacks and drinks on board while watching the sky turn golden over Diamond Head. In August, look for spinner dolphins and flying fish.

meals.breakfast: Leonard's Bakery in Honolulu — legendary malasadas (Portuguese donuts) fresh and hot, a must-try Hawaii experience (~$5–10/person).
meals.lunch: Ala Moana Food Court — wide variety of local and international options including poke, Japanese bento, and Hawaiian plate lunches (~$10–18/person).
meals.dinner: Light pupus (appetizers) and drinks are typically included on the catamaran sunset sail. Afterward, grab a post-cruise dessert at Waikiki's Honolulu Cookie Company or Dave's Ice Cream.

day_by_day.notes: Bishop Museum admission is approximately $26/adult and $19/child. Book the catamaran sunset sail in advance — companies like Maita'i Catamaran or Na Hoku II are popular and family-friendly (~$45–75/person). The sail typically departs from Waikiki Beach and lasts 1.5–2 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Hanauma Bay for a second snorkeling session — now that you know the layout, venture further into the bay to explore the deeper Keyhole and Witches Brew areas. Spot parrotfish, humuhumunukunukuapua'a (Hawaii's state fish), and possibly a sea turtle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Makapu'u Point Lighthouse Trail — a paved 2-mile round-trip coastal hike with stunning views of the windward coast, offshore islands, and during certain seasons, humpback whales. The trail is stroller-accessible and suitable for all ages.
day_by_day.evening: Luau Dinner at Paradise Cove — Experience an authentic Hawaiian luau right on the beachfront with traditional hula dancing, fire knife performances, imu (underground oven) ceremony, and an all-you-can-eat Hawaiian feast. A perfect family evening celebration.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or stop at a local café — try Boots & Kimo's in Kailua for their famous macadamia nut pancakes if you have time (~$12–18/person).
meals.lunch: Zippy's — Hawaii's beloved local chain, perfect for a quick and affordable lunch of saimin noodles, chili, and plate lunches (~$8–15/person).
meals.dinner: Included in the Paradise Cove Luau package — traditional Hawaiian buffet with kalua pig, poi, lomi salmon, haupia, and more (~$110–140/adult, $75–85/child, book in advance).

day_by_day.notes: Paradise Cove Luau is located in Ko Olina on the west side of Oahu (~45-minute drive). Book well in advance as it sells out, especially on weekends. Shuttle transportation from Waikiki is available. The luau runs approximately 5:00–9:00 PM. Bring a light layer as it can be breezy on the beach at night.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Polynesian Cultural Center in Laie on the North Shore — a world-class living museum featuring six authentic Polynesian villages (Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and Aotearoa). Participate in cultural demonstrations, canoe rides, and hands-on activities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center. Watch the spectacular IMAX film on Polynesian navigation and catch the afternoon canoe pageant on the lagoon. Shop for authentic Pacific Island crafts and gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the Ha: Breath of Life evening show at the Polynesian Cultural Center — a stunning theatrical production featuring over 100 Polynesian performers, fire dancers, and acrobats telling the story of a Polynesian boy's journey to manhood.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab pastries and coffee to go before the drive (~$8–12/person).
meals.lunch: Gateway Buffet at the Polynesian Cultural Center — included in most package options, featuring Pacific Island cuisine and Hawaiian favorites.
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau or the evening show dinner package at the Polynesian Cultural Center — traditional Hawaiian feast included with the Ha show package (~$120–160/adult, $85–110/child).

day_by_day.notes: The Polynesian Cultural Center is approximately 35 miles from East Oahu (about 60 minutes). Purchase combo packages online in advance for the best value — the All-Inclusive Ambassador Package includes everything. Plan for a full day (10:00 AM–9:30 PM). The center is run by Brigham Young University Hawaii and has a family-friendly, wholesome atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Pearl Harbor Historic Sites — Visit the USS Arizona Memorial, the Battleship Missouri, and the Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum. A deeply moving and historically significant experience for the whole family. Arrive early as the free Arizona Memorial boat tours fill up quickly.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Pearl Harbor, head to Chinatown in downtown Honolulu. Explore the vibrant open-air markets, art galleries, and cultural shops. Visit the Oahu Market and pick up tropical fruits, fresh flowers, and local snacks. Walk through the historic district and admire the architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed final full-day evening back in East Oahu. Enjoy a beachside sunset walk near Hanauma Bay and a leisurely dinner at a local favorite.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departing for Pearl Harbor. Or grab malasadas and coffee from a drive-through bakery on the way.
meals.lunch: Pearl Harbor Café on site — convenient and reasonably priced sandwiches, salads, and Hawaiian plates (~$12–18/person).
meals.dinner: Roy's Hawaii Kai — James Beard Award-winning chef Roy Yamaguchi's flagship restaurant near the hotel, featuring Hawaiian fusion cuisine with fresh local ingredients. A special splurge-worthy dinner to celebrate the trip (~$45–70/person).

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor is free to enter but the USS Arizona Memorial boat tour is first-come, first-served (arrive by 7:00–8:00 AM) or reserve timed-entry tickets online in advance. The Battleship Missouri and Aviation Museum charge separate admission (~$30–35/person each). Allow 4–5 hours for a thorough visit. No bags larger than a small purse are allowed at Pearl Harbor — use the paid storage lockers at the entrance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Hanauma Bay area — since it's Tuesday the bay is closed, so take a peaceful sunrise walk along the coastal trail near the hotel. Collect shells, take final photos, and soak in the last views of East Oahu's dramatic coastline. Pack up and check out of the boutique stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, stop at the Waikiki area for last-minute souvenir shopping at the International Market Place or along Kalakaua Avenue. Visit the Royal Hawaiian Center for local artisan goods, Aloha shirts, and Hawaiian jewelry. Grab a final shave ice or malasada.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport for departure. Allow 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in, security, and the drive from East Oahu to Daniel K. Inouye International Airport.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or a beloved local spot — try Café Kaila in Market City Shopping Center for creative breakfast dishes and fresh-squeezed juices (~$15–22/person).
meals.lunch: Ono Seafood in Honolulu — tiny, beloved poke shop with some of the freshest poke on the island. Perfect light final meal (~$12–18/person).
meals.dinner: Airport dining or pack snacks for the flight home. Grab a plate lunch box from a nearby deli to enjoy at the gate.

day_by_day.notes: Check your airline's departure time and work backward to plan the day. The drive from East Oahu to the airport takes 25–40 minutes depending on traffic (allow more time during afternoon rush hour). Return your rental car with a full tank of gas — there are gas stations near the airport. Don't forget to declare any fresh fruit, plants, or agricultural items at customs. Mahalo for an amazing Hawaii trip!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Hawaii Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most iconic marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with colorful fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters and equipment rentals on-site. An educational visitor center teaches about the reef ecosystem before you enter.

experiences.name: Luau Dinner at Paradise Cove
experiences.description: Experience an authentic Hawaiian luau right on the beachfront with traditional hula dancing, fire knife performances, and a feast of local dishes including kalua pig, poi, and fresh tropical fruits. A magical cultural evening the whole family will remember, with activities like canoe rides and lei making before the show.

experiences.name: Catamaran Sunset Sail with Whale Watching
experiences.description: Board a family-friendly catamaran for a breathtaking sunset cruise along the Waikiki coastline. During winter and spring months, spot humpback whales breaching offshore. The crew provides snacks, drinks, and narration about Hawaiian marine life, making it both entertaining and educational for children and adults alike.

experiences.name: North Shore Shrimp Trucks and Beach Day
experiences.description: Spend a full day on Oahu's legendary North Shore, starting with a stop at the famous roadside shrimp trucks for garlic butter shrimp plates — a beloved local food tradition. Then relax on the wide sandy shores of Sunset Beach or Waimea Bay, where gentle summer waves are perfect for family swimming and building sandcastles.

experiences.name: Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach
experiences.description: Take a beginner group surfing lesson with certified instructors right on the gentle waves of Waikiki, considered the birthplace of modern surfing. Lessons are tailored for all ages including young children, and most first-timers stand up on their board within the first session. Boards and rash guards are included in the price.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — No morning activities scheduled. Flight LH lands at 1:00 PM. Private luxury transfer from Honolulu International Airport to Hanauma Bay, East Oahu Boutique Stay. Settle into your suite, unpack, and enjoy a welcome amenity prepared by the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: After check-in, take a leisurely stroll along the scenic coastal path near Hanauma Bay to decompress from travel. Enjoy the stunning ocean views and get oriented with the surroundings. The hotel concierge will brief the family on the week's planned experiences.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed first evening at the resort. Enjoy a private beachfront sunset viewing arranged by the hotel, followed by a curated welcome dinner at the boutique stay's oceanview terrace or a nearby acclaimed restaurant.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or at airport lounge — not applicable
meals.lunch: Light refreshments and welcome snacks provided upon hotel arrival
meals.dinner: Roy's Hawaii Kai — A celebrated Hawaii Regional Cuisine restaurant just minutes from Hanauma Bay, offering fresh local seafood, wagyu beef, and stunning ocean views. Perfect for a luxurious first evening.

day_by_day.notes: Request early check-in if possible. Ask the concierge to pre-book all upcoming experiences immediately upon arrival. Ensure sunscreen, reef-safe products, and snorkel gear are ready for Day 2. Private airport transfer should be pre-arranged before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — Begin the day early (reserve entry tickets in advance as spots are limited). Explore one of Hawaii's most iconic marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with colorful tropical fish, sea turtles, and vibrant coral reefs. Opt for a private guided snorkeling tour for the family for a premium, educational experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the boutique stay for a relaxed poolside lunch. Afterward, enjoy a private beach cabana session arranged by the hotel near the bay. Kids can build sandcastles while adults sip on fresh tropical cocktails. Optional: rent paddleboards or kayaks through the hotel for gentle afternoon exploration.
day_by_day.evening: Luau Dinner at Paradise Cove — Experience an authentic Hawaiian luau on the beachfront with traditional hula dancing, fire knife performances, imu (underground oven) pig roasting, and live Hawaiian music. A magical, immersive cultural evening for the whole family.

meals.breakfast: In-room private breakfast service — fresh tropical fruit platters, acai bowls, eggs Benedict, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Poolside dining at the boutique stay — grilled mahi-mahi tacos, shrimp poke bowls, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Paradise Cove Luau — All-inclusive luau feast with traditional kalua pig, poi, lomi lomi salmon, haupia coconut dessert, and open bar

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance online reservations — book at least 2 days ahead. Arrive at the bay by 7:00–8:00 AM for the best experience before crowds build. Reef-safe sunscreen is mandatory at Hanauma Bay. The luau typically begins at sunset; arrange private transport to Paradise Cove (approx. 30 min from East Oahu).

day_by_day.morning: Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach — Drive approximately 20 minutes to Waikiki for a private family surfing lesson with certified instructors. The gentle, rolling waves of Waikiki are ideal for beginners of all ages. A private lesson ensures personalized attention and maximum fun for kids and adults alike.
day_by_day.afternoon: After surfing, explore the upscale Waikiki strip. Visit the iconic Royal Hawaiian Hotel (the 'Pink Palace of the Pacific') for afternoon cocktails on their beachfront terrace. Browse luxury boutiques along Kalakaua Avenue — Chanel, Louis Vuitton, Tiffany & Co. — or visit the International Market Place's premium shopping collection.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner in Waikiki with panoramic ocean views. Return to East Oahu via private car.

meals.breakfast: The Nook Neighborhood Bistro (East Oahu) — artisan pastries, avocado toast, and freshly brewed Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Beachhouse at the Moana (Waikiki) — oceanfront dining with fresh catch of the day, lobster bisque, and tropical salads
meals.dinner: Orchids at the Halekulani Hotel (Waikiki) — AAA Four Diamond oceanfront fine dining featuring contemporary Hawaiian cuisine, fresh local seafood, and an award-winning wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book private surf lessons at least 48 hours in advance. Children as young as 5 can participate in surf lessons at Waikiki. Apply reef-safe sunscreen generously before lessons. Waikiki is approximately 20–25 minutes from Hanauma Bay by car.

day_by_day.morning: Catamaran Sunset Sail with Whale Watching (Morning Departure Option) — Board a family-friendly luxury catamaran for a breathtaking cruise along the Waikiki coastline. Spot spinner dolphins, sea turtles, and possibly humpback whales (sightings vary by season). Enjoy snacks and drinks onboard while the kids delight in marine wildlife.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Diamond Head State Monument — hike the iconic volcanic crater trail (approximately 1.6 miles round trip) for panoramic views of Honolulu and the Pacific Ocean. The trail is family-friendly with moderate difficulty. Afterward, cool off at nearby Kaimana Beach (San Souci Beach), a quieter, less crowded gem beloved by locals.
day_by_day.evening: Catamaran Sunset Sail (if preferred in the evening instead) — alternatively, enjoy a private beachfront dinner at the boutique stay or a nearby East Oahu gem. Watch the sun dip into the Pacific from your hotel terrace.

meals.breakfast: In-room service — smoothie bowls, macadamia nut pancakes, fresh papaya, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch box prepared by the hotel for Diamond Head hike — artisan sandwiches, tropical fruit, sparkling water, and chocolate macadamia nut cookies
meals.dinner: Mariposa at Neiman Marcus (Ala Moana) or 12th Ave Grill (Kaimuki, near East Oahu) — celebrated farm-to-table cuisine featuring locally sourced ingredients and exceptional service

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head hike opens at 6:00 AM; arrive early to avoid midday heat and crowds. Bring plenty of water and sun protection. The catamaran experience is best booked for either a morning wildlife cruise or a classic sunset sail — confirm preference with the concierge. August is outside peak humpback season, but spinner dolphins are commonly seen year-round.

day_by_day.morning: North Shore Shrimp Trucks and Beach Day — Embark on a scenic full-day private driver tour to Oahu's legendary North Shore. Stop at the famous roadside shrimp trucks (Giovanni's, Fumi's) for a quintessential local experience. Visit Haleiwa town for shave ice at Matsumoto's and browse charming surf boutiques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Sunset Beach or Waimea Bay — two of the world's most famous surf beaches. In summer, the waters are calm and perfect for swimming and snorkeling. Walk to Waimea Valley for a lush botanical garden hike ending at a stunning freshwater waterfall where kids can swim.
day_by_day.evening: Return to East Oahu via private car along the scenic Kamehameha Highway. Enjoy a relaxed dinner near the boutique stay.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure — eggs, fresh fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: North Shore Shrimp Trucks — garlic butter shrimp plates, coconut shrimp, and fresh lemonade (a beloved local institution)
meals.dinner: Koko Head Café (East Honolulu) — acclaimed brunch-style dinner with creative, locally inspired dishes, or room service at the boutique stay for a relaxed family evening

day_by_day.notes: Hire a private driver or luxury SUV for the North Shore day trip for maximum comfort and flexibility. The drive from East Oahu to the North Shore takes approximately 1 hour. Waimea Valley charges a small entrance fee; book in advance. Summer North Shore waves are gentle — ideal for family swimming.

day_by_day.morning: Private Snorkeling Charter — Book a private luxury snorkeling boat charter departing from Hawaii Kai Marina (minutes from the boutique stay). Explore hidden sea caves, pristine reefs, and snorkel alongside sea turtles in secluded spots inaccessible from shore. The private charter ensures an exclusive, unhurried experience for the family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Sea Life Park Hawaii (Makapu'u, East Oahu — 15 minutes away) — a fantastic family-friendly marine park featuring dolphin encounters, penguin feedings, sea turtle exhibits, and shark encounters. Kids will love the interactive experiences. Opt for the premium dolphin swim program for an unforgettable memory.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the boutique stay. Enjoy a private in-suite dinner or a sunset cocktail hour on your terrace overlooking the bay.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — loco moco (Hawaiian rice, hamburger patty, egg, and gravy), fresh pineapple, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Onboard the private charter — gourmet picnic spread with charcuterie, fresh sushi rolls, tropical fruits, and chilled beverages
meals.dinner: In-room private chef experience — arrange through the hotel concierge for a local private chef to prepare a Hawaiian tasting menu in your suite (poke, fresh fish, haupia dessert)

day_by_day.notes: Book the private snorkeling charter and Sea Life Park dolphin swim well in advance — these premium experiences fill up quickly in August. Hawaii Kai Marina is the closest departure point to the boutique stay. Sea Life Park is approximately 15 minutes from Hanauma Bay.

day_by_day.morning: Helicopter Tour of Oahu — Experience the island from above with a luxury private helicopter tour. Fly over Diamond Head, the Ko'olau Mountains, Hanauma Bay, the Windward Coast, and the stunning Nuuanu Pali cliffs. A breathtaking, once-in-a-lifetime perspective of Hawaii's dramatic landscape that the entire family will treasure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Polynesian Cultural Center (approximately 1 hour from East Oahu on the Windward Coast) — an expansive living museum celebrating the cultures of Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and New Zealand. Interactive villages, canoe rides, and cultural demonstrations make it ideal for families.
day_by_day.evening: Ha: Breath of Life Show at the Polynesian Cultural Center — a spectacular evening theatrical production featuring 100 performers, fire dancing, and the story of a Polynesian family across generations. Dinner included in the premium package.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the early helicopter departure — yogurt parfaits, granola, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Hukilau Marketplace at the Polynesian Cultural Center — sample authentic dishes from multiple Polynesian cultures including Samoan chop suey, Hawaiian laulau, and Tongan desserts
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau Dinner at the Polynesian Cultural Center — included with the Ha: Breath of Life premium package; features a grand Hawaiian buffet

day_by_day.notes: Book the helicopter tour at least one week in advance; Blue Hawaiian Helicopters offers premium private tours from Honolulu. Weight limits apply for helicopter tours — confirm details during booking. The Polynesian Cultural Center is approximately 1 hour from East Oahu; arrange private transport. Premium packages include priority seating for the evening show.

day_by_day.morning: Spa and Wellness Morning — Enjoy a family spa morning at a nearby luxury spa (the hotel concierge can arrange in-suite treatments or transport to the Kahala Hotel & Resort Spa, one of Oahu's finest). Adults enjoy signature Hawaiian lomilomi massages while kids enjoy gentle spa treatments designed for younger guests.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kailua Beach on the Windward Coast (approximately 30 minutes from East Oahu) — consistently ranked among America's best beaches, with powdery white sand and turquoise calm waters. Rent premium paddleboards or kayak to the Mokulua Islands (the 'Mokes') for a spectacular offshore adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Catamaran Sail — If not taken earlier in the trip, this is the perfect evening for the luxury catamaran sunset cruise along the Waikiki coastline. Watch the sky turn gold and pink over the Pacific with champagne in hand.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — banana macadamia nut French toast, fresh açaí bowls, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Buzz's Original Steakhouse (Kailua) — a beloved Kailua institution since 1962, offering fresh fish, prime steaks, and a relaxed beachside ambiance
meals.dinner: Catamaran onboard appetizers and champagne during sunset sail, followed by dinner at Taormina Sicilian Cuisine (Waikiki) — acclaimed Italian-Hawaiian fusion in an intimate setting

day_by_day.notes: Lomilomi massage is a traditional Hawaiian healing practice — a meaningful cultural experience. Kailua Beach paddleboard and kayak rentals are available through premium operators; book in advance. The Mokulua Islands kayak trip is approximately 1.5 miles offshore — suitable for families with older children.

day_by_day.morning: Private Guided Hike in Ko'olau Mountains — Embark on a private guided nature hike through Oahu's stunning Ko'olau Range, exploring lush rainforest trails, dramatic ridgelines, and hidden waterfalls. A certified local guide will share the history, flora, and legends of the Hawaiian mountains. Choose a family-appropriate trail based on fitness level.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bishop Museum (Honolulu) — Hawaii's premier natural and cultural history museum, featuring the world's largest collection of Polynesian artifacts, a stunning planetarium, and engaging exhibits perfect for curious young minds. The Science Adventure Center is a highlight for families.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell pre-celebration dinner at one of Honolulu's finest restaurants — a special evening to reflect on the incredible week and celebrate the family's Hawaii adventure.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast — scrambled eggs with smoked salmon, fresh tropical fruit, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by the hotel for the mountain hike — gourmet sandwiches, local cheeses, macadamia nut trail mix, and chilled coconut water
meals.dinner: Senia (Chinatown, Honolulu) — one of Hawaii's most celebrated fine dining restaurants, offering a creative tasting menu of locally sourced Hawaiian ingredients with global technique; James Beard Award-nominated chefs

day_by_day.notes: Book the private hiking guide at least 3 days in advance. Trail selection should account for children's ages and fitness levels — the guide can recommend appropriate routes. The Bishop Museum is approximately 25 minutes from East Oahu. Senia requires reservations well in advance — book before the trip begins.

day_by_day.morning: Final Morning at Hanauma Bay — One last sunrise snorkel or beach walk at the iconic Hanauma Bay to soak in the beauty of East Oahu. Collect shells, take final photos, and say goodbye to the sea turtles. Return to the boutique stay for a leisurely checkout experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time: Visit the Aloha Stadium Swap Meet for last-minute authentic Hawaiian souvenirs, or browse luxury Hawaiian brands (Sig Zane, Manaola) in Honolulu. Stop at a local bakery for malasadas (Leonard's Bakery — a Honolulu institution) as a sweet farewell treat. Private luxury transfer to Honolulu International Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — Aloha! Carry the spirit of Hawaii home with unforgettable memories of beaches, culture, family adventures, and world-class luxury.

meals.breakfast: Special farewell breakfast at the boutique stay — full Hawaiian spread with fresh pineapple, loco moco, lilikoi (passion fruit) juice, and macadamia nut waffles
meals.lunch: Helena's Hawaiian Food (Honolulu) — a James Beard Award-winning institution serving authentic Hawaiian comfort food including pipikaula short ribs, poi, and chicken long rice
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight — request premium in-flight meals in advance; alternatively, dine at the Daniel K. Inouye Airport's better dining options before departure

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the boutique stay and arrange luggage storage if needed for afternoon activities. Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for airport check-in and security. Purchase reef-safe sunscreen, Kona coffee, macadamia nuts, and Hawaiian honey as premium gifts to bring home. Request a late checkout if the flight departs in the evening.
